articles.headline: OFAC Designates Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations for Narcotics and Terrorism
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated three Guatemalan criminal organizations for their involvement in narcotics trafficking and terrorism. The designations target the 'Los Lorenzana,' 'Los Mendoza,' and 'Los Huistas' drug trafficking organizations.

Specifically, OFAC imposed blocking sanctions against the Los Mendoza Drug Trafficking Organization under Executive Orders 14059 and 13224 for supporting the Sinaloa Cartel. The counterterrorism authority was also added to the existing narcotics designation for the Los Huistas Drug Trafficking Organization due to its support for both the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG.

The State Department concurrently designated Los Lorenzanas as a Foreign Terrorist Organization under section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act and as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist under Executive Order 13224.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Sanctions Expert Feed

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Sanctions List, Targets Shipping Services
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced an update to its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List concerning Iran. This action specifically targets entities involved in facilitating Iranian shipping services.
The update includes changes to the listing for VOLTA SHIPPING SERVICES LLC, which is also known as VOLTA SHIPPING SERVICES FZCO and VOLTA CONTAINER LINE FZCO.
These entities, located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, are now linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani and carry secondary sanctions risk under Section 2 of Executive Order 13902.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Eight Canadian Money Services Businesses for Enabling Iranian Regime
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated eight Canada-based money services businesses (MSBs) for operating in the digital asset sector of the Iranian economy.

These businesses are accused of exchanging Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, with many reportedly dealing with sanctioned Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges and digital asset addresses linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

The action, part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' aims to disrupt financial channels supporting the Iranian regime and follows previous rounds of Iran-related sanctions targeting the digital asset sector.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations; Issues Cuba-related Determination
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations. This action also includes new designations related to Cuba and the publication of a Cuba-related determination.

These designations aim to combat illicit activities that pose a threat to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests, including those involving malicious cyber operations and international criminal networks.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, as well as the nature of the Cuba-related determination, are available on OFAC's recent actions page.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-related Designations, Amends Venezuela GL, and Issues Iran Alert
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations, alongside updates to existing Iran-related listings.
As part of this action, OFAC also published an Iran-related alert and issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a related Frequently Asked Question.

The Iran-related measures target networks accused of providing fraudulent vessel flags and maritime certifications to Iran's 'shadow fleet,' and a Türkiye-based company supporting sanctioned Iranian airlines.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License FF-1
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Iran General License FF-1, titled 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.'
This amended general license provides authorization for transactions that are ordinarily incident and necessary to the wind down of dealings with the specified bank.
The issuance of General License FF-1 is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to manage and adjust its sanctions programs related to Iran.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Individuals and Entities for North Korea and DRC-Related Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in activities related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

The North Korea-related additions include Russian and North Korean nationals linked to LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ALIS, CHINYONG INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY COOPERATION COMPANY, and FIRST FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT CENTER.
The DRC-related designations include Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a Kigali-based financial institution, for their alleged support of the M23 rebel group.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a $1,529,685 settlement with Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider.

The settlement resolves nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and services to Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer.
MMZA was majority-owned by the designated JSC Concern Almaz Antey, making it a blocked person by operation of law, even though MMZA itself was not directly listed on the SDN List until June 2022.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Corruption, Crime & Compliance

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has amended several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) as part of its ongoing review of published guidance.
The updated FAQs, specifically numbers 10, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, address topics related to blocking and rejecting transactions, as well as filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments aim to ensure that the information provided to the public remains current and clear, particularly concerning compliance obligations for financial institutions and other U.S. persons.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations. This action also includes removals of designations related to Belarus and North Korea.
In addition, OFAC has issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, along with amended Frequently Asked Questions.
These measures reflect OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, adjusting to evolving geopolitical landscapes and specific policy objectives across various programs.

articles.headline: UK Updates Sanctions List with Additions and Variations for Russia Regime
body: On November 12, 2026, the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office updated the UK Sanctions List on GOV.UK with 20 additions and 1 variation under the Russia (EU Exit) (Sanctions) Regulations 2019.
The additions include entities and individuals deemed to be involved in obtaining a benefit from or supporting the Government of Russia, particularly in the Russian energy sector.

New transport and trade sanctions apply to specified ships, prohibiting them from entering UK ports, being chartered or operated, or receiving various services if they are involved in carrying Russian oil or oil products.

The settlement addresses nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The violations involved the export of networking equipment and related services to a Russian defense manufacturer that was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by a designated entity.

articles.headline: Commerce Department Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR).
This deregulatory action shifts control from the State Department's U.S. Munitions List, aligning export controls on suppressors with those already applied to firearms.
The change aims to streamline the export process for these items while maintaining appropriate national security safeguards.

articles.headline: BIS Closes Export Controls Loophole for Foreign-Owned Semiconductor Fabs in China
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has closed a loophole that previously allowed a handful of foreign companies to export semiconductor manufacturing equipment and technology to China license-free.
These foreign-owned semiconductor fabrication facilities in China will now be required to obtain licenses to export their technology, placing them on par with their competitors.
This action aims to strengthen U.S. export controls and prevent advanced technology from being used to undermine national security interests.

articles.headline: BIS Extends Suspension of 'Affiliates Rule' Until January 10, 2027
body: The U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has extended the suspension of its 'Affiliates Rule' from November 10, 2026, through January 10, 2027.

The Affiliates Rule, issued in September 2025, would expand export control restrictions under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to non-U.S. entities that are 50 percent or more owned by parties on the BIS Entity List, Military End-User List, and certain Specially Designated Nationals.

This extension provides companies with additional time to review screening procedures, update trade compliance programs, and enhance due diligence on foreign suppliers, customers, and distributors to prepare for the rule's eventual implementation.

articles.headline: Extension of the Suspension of Expansion of End-User Controls for Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities

The suspension was set to end November 9, 2026. This final rule extends the suspension through January 10, 2027.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
